text: Vhalin Bay, July 18 — The Marisol Trench probe reached a depth of 9,400 metres during its latest descent, people familiar with the matter said, topping the mission’s previous record by 180 metres. The uncrewed craft, operated by the private Pelagos Deepwater Institute, transmitted stable pressure and temperature readings for 11 minutes at the floor before initiating an automated ascent, according to the people. Engineers said the probe’s titanium housing held intact and that the vehicle recovered usable sonar maps from a 3-kilometre stretch of seabed. A final technical review is expected later this week, with researchers planning a second dive after software adjustments to the descent thrusters, the people said.
